newsitem.title: USA: Key House lawmakers aim to pass power bill in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Key House lawmakers aim to pass power bill in 1997.

text.p: In a show of bipartisan cooperation, key U.S. House lawmakers said Wednesday they hoped to pass a bill this year to make states open their power markets to competition.
"We hope to get it done this year," said House Commerce Committee Chairman Thomas Bliley, R-Va.
He said the House last year defied expectations that it would fail to pass legislation to deregulate the telecommunications market, revise food safety and safe drinking water regulations.
"We can do this too," he said at a news conference with House energy and power subcommittee chairman Dan Schaefer, a Colorado Republican, and Ed Markey, a Massachusetts Democrat.
Markey, a senior Democrat on the Commerce Committee, who wants to open the market to competition without forcing the states to do so, predicted a bill would pass this year.
"I'm very confident that under the leadership of Tom Bliley and Dan Schaefer that we will be able to work together to fashion legislation this year," he said.
Breaking up utility monopolies would be hard, Bliley said, but he predicted a bill would pass with bipartisan support.
"When the time comes, we will have more than 218 votes," he said, referring to the majority needed to pass a bill in the House.
Schaefer and Bliley plan to hold about a half dozen public hearings around the country on the issue, before debating legislation.
Schaefer reintroduced a bill Monday that would require states to give all consumers freedom to choose their power suppliers by December 15, 2000.

Among the key issues that had to be addressed, Bliley said Congress would have to decide how to handle public power utilities, including the Tennessee Valley Authority and the Bonneville Power Administration, which are major suppliers of cheap power in their areas.
